newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit hits weakest level vs dlr since flotation.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit hits weakest level vs dlr since flotation.

text.p: The ringgit hit its lowest post-flotation level against the dollar on Friday as offshore players stepped up selling of the Malaysian currency, dealers said.
At 0515 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.8080/110 to a dollar after hitting 2.8200, its weakest level since the currency was officially floated in 1973.
"Trading volume is thin which makes it easy to move the market. Not much is actually going through," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
But further upside in the dollar was limited by profit-taking activities, he said.
"Many have been looking to take profits above 2.80," the dealer said.
Dealers said the fresh selling in the ringgit was triggered by weakness in the Indonesian rupiah which dropped to a record low of 2,890 to the dollar on Friday.
The rupiah was further pressured after Bank of Indonesia scrapped the daily announcements of its conversion and intervention bands on Thursday.
The action by the Indonesian central bank is seen as amounting to a managed float of the rupiah.
